name: Send Slack alerts for new npm package releases with Apify

nodes.name: Only the releases you asked for

parameters.content:
## Send Slack alerts for new npm and PyPI releases with Apify

Watches the packages you depend on and tells you when one ships — but only the releases you actually care about, not every patch bump on every dependency.

**Who is this for?**
Anyone maintaining a project whose dependencies move faster than they can read release notes.

**What problem is this workflow solving?**
Watching a repo on GitHub gets you everything or nothing. A five-package watchlist can fire twenty times a week, almost all of it patch releases nobody needs to read, and the one breaking major gets lost in the noise.

**What this workflow does**
- Checks your watchlist on npm or PyPI every 12 hours.
- Skips versions already seen in an earlier run.
- Reads the version number and decides whether it is a major, a minor, a patch or a pre-release.
- Keeps only the bump types you listed and anything above your download floor.
- Posts what is left to Slack.

**Setup**
1. Add an Apify credential and a Slack credential.
2. Put your packages in "Packages to watch" and set `registry` to `npm` or `pypi`.
3. Set `watchBumps` — `major` alone for breaking changes only, `major,minor` to also hear about new features.
4. Set `minMonthlyDownloads` if you only care about widely-used packages. 0 watches everything.

**Requirements**
An Apify account and API token, and a Slack workspace you can post to. No GitHub token and no registry account — the release data is public.

**How to customize this workflow to your needs**

Four nodes sit under the main row, wired to nothing on purpose. Connect the filter to whichever you want and delete the rest:

- **Discord** — post to a channel instead of Slack, or as well as.
- **Gmail** — mail releases to yourself.
- **Notion** — keep a changelog page of everything that shipped.
- **HTTP Request** — send the release to your own endpoint.

The classifier is a Code node, not a model, so the rules are readable and yours to change. Registries that do not follow semver are the obvious reason to edit it.

**Good to know**
The bump type comes from the version number alone, which is what the registry publishes and all it publishes. A project that ships a breaking change in a patch release will be labelled a patch, because nothing in the version says otherwise. Anything below 1.0.0 is flagged pre-stable for the same reason — the numbers there promise nothing.

### 1. Schedule
Every 12 hours. Daily is cheaper and usually fast enough; hourly is for a dependency you are actively waiting on.

### 2. Your input
The packages to watch and which registry they live in. This is the only node you have to edit.

### 3. Check
Looks up the current version of each package. Add your Apify credential here. Max cost per run is capped at $1.

### 4. Clean
Drops the uncharged diagnostic row returned when a package name does not exist.

### 5. Dedupe
Keyed on name plus version, so an unchanged package is silent and only a real release gets through.

### 8. Deliver

Slack gets the releases that made it through. Swap in one of the nodes below if Slack is not where you want them.

### 6. Classify it

Reads the version number and decides whether it is a major, a minor, a patch or a pre-release. Plain JavaScript you can edit — no model, no API key.

### 7. Only what you asked for

Keeps the bump types listed in `watchBumps` and anything at or above your download floor. Majors only, on popular packages, is one edit away.

## Optional — drag a connection into any of these

They are wired to nothing on purpose. Connect the filter above to whichever ones you want and delete the rest. Discord and Slack both work; so does keeping a Notion changelog and posting to your own webhook at the same time.
